identity.name: The Gentlemen 'GentleKiller' ThrottleStop.sys BYOVD EDR-Kill — Cortex EDR Behavioral Anomaly (ABIOC) (T1562.001 / T1543.003 / T1068)
identity.summary: The Gentlemen conduct BYOVD EDR-kill with the signed-but-vulnerable ThrottleStop.sys driver (CVE-2025-7771) to reach kernel context and blind the EDR sensor — consistent with the crew's GentleKiller tradecraft — then run Advanced IP Scanner recon, a SystemBC beacon, and vssadmin/wmic shadow-copy deletion. The ABIOC anchors the driver-load-to-telemetry-gap chain as citable forensic evidence.
identity.description: Bring-Your-Own-Vulnerable-Driver (BYOVD) EDR-kill is the defining move of The Gentlemen ransomware intrusions documented by Unit 42. Unit 42 attributes an 'EDR killer framework' (GentleKiller) to the crew and separately flags the vulnerable driver ThrottleStop.sys (CVE-2025-7771); modeling those two findings as one mechanism is an analyst inference the report does not state outright. On that inference, a GentleKiller-class loader registers a kernel-driver service for the signed-but-vulnerable ThrottleStop.sys and loads it to gain an arbitrary kernel read/write primitive that terminates or blinds endpoint-security processes from ring 0. Because a validly signed driver carries no known-bad hash, no IOC and no static allow/deny signature catches the load; the malicious act is the CONTEXT (a rare, vulnerable OEM driver loaded by a non-standard process on a host whose learned driver baseline has never seen it) and its CONSEQUENCE (the host's own Cortex telemetry stream collapses seconds later). That deviation-plus-causality is exactly what an auto-tuned Analytics Behavioral IOC (ABIOC) is built to fire on. This card models the full Gentlemen chain as a connected causality graph: (1) a driver service / registry ImagePath is written for ThrottleStop.sys (T1543.003), (2) the signed-vulnerable driver is loaded into the kernel (T1068), (3) the Cortex sensor's per-host event stream drops — the t0 tamper (T1562.001), (4) a _gentlemen*-named scheduled task is created for persistence (T1053.005), (5) Advanced IP Scanner sweeps the internal subnet and a SystemBC beacon calls out over a non-standard port (T1046 / T1571), (6) vssadmin/wmic delete Volume Shadow Copies to inhibit recovery (T1490), before ransomware impact (T1485). A terminal ABIOC anchors the vulnerable-driver-load deviation to the sensor-telemetry gap, a second ABIOC anchors the post-tamper hands-on-keyboard burst on the blinded host, and a correlation rule stitches every stage into a single incident whose evidence graph — registry write, signed-driver load, telemetry gap, scheduled task, scanner + beacon, shadow-copy deletion — is exported verbatim as the POV's citable forensic packet. This is the F10 'the qualitative evidence tells the whole story' proof: behavioral-ML catches what the signed driver defeats at the signature layer, and the causality chain gives the SOC a court-ready timeline.

execution.framework_reference_id: SIM-EDR-021 — The Gentlemen GentleKiller ThrottleStop.sys BYOVD EDR-kill behavioral-anomaly chain for Cortex ABIOC + forensic-evidence validation (non-destructive, SAFE-MODE markers).

prerequisites.description: Cortex XDR / XSIAM Windows agent installed on the target so per-host driver-load, registry, process, scheduled-task and sensor-health telemetry reaches xdr_data.
A baseline window has elapsed during which the host loaded only its normal signed driver set so Cortex learned the per-host driver-load profile the ABIOC deviates from.

payload.code:
# NON-DESTRUCTIVE SAFE-MODE. No driver is installed or loaded, no process is
# terminated, no C2 egress occurs, and no shadow copies are deleted. Each stage
# writes an inert marker describing the modeled Gentlemen GentleKiller behavior
# so Cortex sees the telemetry SHAPE without any real impact.
$stage = Join-Path $env:TEMP 'cortexsim-edr-021'
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $stage | Out-Null
Set-Content -Path (Join-Path $stage 'SAFE-MODE-throttlestop-driver-service.marker') -Value 'CortexSim SIM-EDR-021 SAFE-MODE: models a kernel-driver service / registry ImagePath created for the signed-but-vulnerable ThrottleStop.sys (CVE-2025-7771). No driver is registered or loaded.'
Set-Content -Path (Join-Path $stage 'SAFE-MODE-sensor-telemetry-gap.marker') -Value 'CortexSim SIM-EDR-021 SAFE-MODE: models the EDR sensor telemetry gap that follows the BYOVD load. Telemetry-shape marker only; the agent is untouched.'
Set-Content -Path (Join-Path $stage 'SAFE-MODE-systembc-c2-and-shadow-deletion.marker') -Value ('CortexSim SIM-EDR-021 SAFE-MODE: models Advanced IP Scanner recon, a SystemBC beacon to {0} on a non-standard port, and vssadmin/wmic shadow-copy deletion. No egress and no deletion occur.' -f $env:STAGE_HOST)
Write-Host 'cortexsim-edr-021-gentlekiller-byovd-chain-modeled'

input_variables.name: STAGE_HOST
input_variables.description: Authorised internal host the modeled SystemBC beacon marker references. No packet is sent in SAFE-MODE.

expected_artifacts.description: A kernel-driver service registry key whose ImagePath points at the signed-but-vulnerable ThrottleStop.sys.
A signed, vulnerable OEM driver (ThrottleStop.sys) loaded into the kernel by a non-standard loader process the host baseline never exhibits.
A scheduled task created with the actor's _gentlemen* naming convention.

biocs.name: GentleKiller Vulnerable Driver Service Created (ThrottleStop.sys BYOVD)
biocs.description: A kernel-driver service is registered (registry ImagePath under Services) pointing at ThrottleStop.sys — the signed-but-vulnerable OEM driver (CVE-2025-7771) The Gentlemen abuse for BYOVD EDR-kill. The service-creation write is the earliest citable forensic artifact of the chain and precedes the actual driver load.
biocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.REGISTRY and event_sub_type = ENUM.REGISTRY_SET_VALUE
| filter action_registry_key_name contains "\\Services\\" and action_registry_value_name = "ImagePath"
| filter lowercase(action_registry_data) contains "throttlestop.sys"
| filter actor_process_image_name not in ("TrustedInstaller.exe", "msiexec.exe")
| fields agent_hostname, actor_process_image_name, action_registry_key_name, action_registry_data

biocs.name: Volume Shadow Copy Deletion via vssadmin/wmic (Pre-Encryption)
biocs.description: vssadmin, wmic, wbadmin or diskshadow deletes or resizes Volume Shadow Copies to inhibit recovery ahead of ransomware encryption — the destructive stage that follows the blinded-host recon and C2 in The Gentlemen chain. A high-fidelity, citable impact artifact for the POV report.
biocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_name in ("vssadmin.exe", "wmic.exe", "wbadmin.exe", "diskshadow.exe")
| filter lowercase(action_process_image_command_line) contains "delete shadows" or lowercase(action_process_image_command_line) contains "shadowcopy delete" or lowercase(action_process_image_command_line) contains "resize shadowstorage"
| comp count() as shadow_ops by agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, action_process_image_name, action_process_image_command_line
| filter shadow_ops >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, action_process_image_name, action_process_image_command_line, shadow_ops

abiocs.name: BYOVD EDR-Kill Behavioral Anomaly — Anomalous Signed Vulnerable Driver Load (GentleKiller)
abiocs.description: The terminal ABIOC of the chain. A signed but vulnerable OEM driver (ThrottleStop.sys, CVE-2025-7771) — validly code-signed, so no known-bad-hash IOC applies — is loaded into the kernel by a non-standard loader process on a host whose learned driver-load baseline has never carried it. The ABIOC fires on the deviation (rare vulnerable driver + unexpected loader + first-seen-on-host) and anchors it to the causality chain driver-service-create -> vulnerable-driver-load -> sensor-telemetry-loss, catching the EDR-kill that the signature layer cannot.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.LOAD_IMAGE and action_module_signature_status = "SIGNED"
| filter lowercase(action_module_path) contains "throttlestop.sys"
| filter actor_process_image_name not in ("services.exe", "wininit.exe", "smss.exe", "TrustedInstaller.exe")
| comp count() as anomalous_driver_loads by agent_hostname, action_module_path, actor_process_image_name
| filter anomalous_driver_loads >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, action_module_path, actor_process_image_name, anomalous_driver_loads
abiocs.causality_anchor: Learned per-host driver-load baseline (a stable set of signed drivers loaded only by services.exe/wininit.exe) -> registry ImagePath write for ThrottleStop.sys -> the signed-vulnerable driver loaded by a non-standard process -> the host's Cortex sensor telemetry stream collapsing within seconds, anchored as one t0-tamper causality chain.

abiocs.name: Post-BYOVD Hands-on-Keyboard Burst on a Blinded Host — Recon and SystemBC C2
abiocs.description: Immediately after the sensor-telemetry gap, the same host exhibits a rapid, out-of-baseline behavioral cluster the learned profile never produced: Advanced IP Scanner internal sweeps, an outbound beacon to a non-standard port matching SystemBC's cadence, and shadow-storage tampering. The ABIOC fires on the breadth-and-cadence deviation of this burst, anchored to the tamper event that immediately precedes it — no single tool here is a known-bad IOC.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 900)
| filter (event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START and action_process_image_name in ("advanced_ip_scanner.exe", "advanced_port_scanner.exe")) or (event_type = ENUM.NETWORK and event_sub_type = ENUM.NETWORK_CONNECTION and action_remote_port not in (80, 443, 53, 8080) and dst_action_external_hostname != null)
| comp count_distinct(action_process_image_name) as recon_tools, count_distinct(action_remote_port) as beacon_ports, count() as burst_events by agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, causality_actor_process_image_name
| filter recon_tools >= 1 and beacon_ports >= 1
| sort desc burst_events
| fields agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, causality_actor_process_image_name, recon_tools, beacon_ports, burst_events
abiocs.causality_anchor: Sensor-telemetry gap on the blinded host -> a burst of distinct discovery/staging utilities (Advanced IP Scanner) plus a non-standard-port SystemBC beacon whose breadth and cadence exceed the host's learned process/network baseline, anchored to the causality process spawned after the BYOVD tamper.

xql_queries.name: GentleKiller Vulnerable Driver Load Preceding EDR Telemetry Loss
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 900)
| filter event_type = ENUM.LOAD_IMAGE and lowercase(action_module_path) contains "throttlestop.sys"
| comp count() as driver_loads by agent_hostname, action_module_path, actor_process_image_name
| filter driver_loads >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, action_module_path, actor_process_image_name, driver_loads

xql_queries.name: GentleKiller Named Scheduled Task Creation (_gentlemen Pattern)
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_name = "schtasks.exe" and lowercase(action_process_image_command_line) contains "/create"
| filter lowercase(action_process_image_command_line) contains "_gentlemen"
| comp count() as task_creations by agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, action_process_image_command_line
| filter task_creations >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, action_process_image_command_line, task_creations

correlation_rules.name: The Gentlemen BYOVD Ransomware Chain — Full Causality Stitch
correlation_rules.logic: Fires when, on the same agent_hostname within the run window, the BIOC `GentleKiller Vulnerable Driver Service Created (ThrottleStop.sys BYOVD)`, the terminal ABIOC `BYOVD EDR-Kill Behavioral Anomaly — Anomalous Signed Vulnerable Driver Load (GentleKiller)`, the ABIOC `Post-BYOVD Hands-on-Keyboard Burst on a Blinded Host — Recon and SystemBC C2`, and the BIOC `Volume Shadow Copy Deletion via vssadmin/wmic (Pre-Encryption)` observe activity. It fuses driver-service-create -> vulnerable-driver-load -> sensor-telemetry-gap -> scheduled-task persistence -> recon + SystemBC C2 -> shadow-copy deletion into ONE Gentlemen-BYOVD-ransomware incident whose ordered evidence graph is exported verbatim as the POV forensic packet.

use_cases.name: BYOVD EDR-Kill Behavioral Detection and Court-Ready Forensic Evidence via Cortex ABIOC
use_cases.description: The Gentlemen defeat the signature layer by loading a signed but vulnerable driver, so the catch has to be behavioral: Cortex's auto-tuned ABIOCs fire on the anomalous driver-load-to-telemetry-loss deviation and the post-tamper hands-on-keyboard burst, and the correlation rule assembles a single incident whose ordered evidence graph the DC exports as the POV's citable forensic packet.

test_cases.objective: The terminal ABIOC and the correlation rule fire on the full BYOVD EDR-kill chain and produce one stitched incident.
preconditions: Windows EDR target with the Cortex agent installed.
Per-host driver-load baseline learned (host never previously loaded ThrottleStop.sys).
steps: Model the driver-service create, the signed-vulnerable driver load, and the sensor-telemetry gap.
Observe the terminal ABIOC fire and CR-EDR-0021 raise a Gentlemen-BYOVD incident.
success_criteria: ABIOC `BYOVD EDR-Kill Behavioral Anomaly — Anomalous Signed Vulnerable Driver Load (GentleKiller)` fires.
Correlation `CR-EDR-0021` raises one stitched BYOVD-ransomware incident.

test_cases.objective: The driver-service-creation and shadow-copy-deletion BIOCs produce citable forensic evidence a POV report can show.
preconditions: Windows EDR target with the Cortex agent installed.
steps: Model the ThrottleStop.sys driver-service registry write and the vssadmin/wmic shadow-copy deletion.
Confirm both BIOCs fire and their evidence rows are exportable.
success_criteria: BIOC `GentleKiller Vulnerable Driver Service Created (ThrottleStop.sys BYOVD)` fires with the registry ImagePath evidence row.
BIOC `Volume Shadow Copy Deletion via vssadmin/wmic (Pre-Encryption)` fires with the command-line evidence row.

test_cases.objective: The post-tamper burst ABIOC and the _gentlemen scheduled-task hunt surface the hands-on-keyboard activity on the blinded host.
preconditions: Windows EDR target with the Cortex agent installed.
steps: Model the _gentlemen* scheduled task, Advanced IP Scanner recon, and the SystemBC beacon.
Confirm the burst ABIOC fires and the scheduled-task hunt returns the task.
success_criteria: ABIOC `Post-BYOVD Hands-on-Keyboard Burst on a Blinded Host — Recon and SystemBC C2` fires.

preventive_controls: Enable Cortex XDR Malicious/Vulnerable Driver Protection and the Microsoft vulnerable-driver blocklist (HVCI) so signed-but-vulnerable drivers such as ThrottleStop.sys (CVE-2025-7771) are blocked at load, not merely detected.
Enforce driver code-integrity / WDAC policies that allow only an approved driver set, denying first-seen OEM utility drivers on servers.
Alert on any kernel-driver service creation whose ImagePath resolves to a user-writable or non-standard path.
detection_engineering: Let Cortex auto-tune ABIOCs against the learned per-host driver-load baseline and sensor-health continuity rather than hand-authoring known-bad-driver hash IOCs the signed driver defeats.
Alert on a host's own Cortex sensor telemetry stream dropping within seconds of a rare/vulnerable driver load — treat the gap itself as signal (T1562.001).
Hunt scheduled tasks matching the _gentlemen* naming convention and correlate Advanced IP Scanner execution with non-standard-port outbound beacons on the same host.
